docs.avatar.a11y.contrast: Every tone pairs initials with their own background, both defined for the light and the dark theme, and each pair passes 4.5:1. A color of your own through className is yours to check.
docs.avatar.a11y.decorative: Pass decorative when the name is written next to the avatar, in a list row or a comment header: the avatar is then hidden from assistive technology with aria-hidden and the name is read once, not twice.
docs.avatar.a11y.name: Unless it is decorative, the avatar is an image (role="img") named after name, so a screen reader reads «Laura Méndez», not the two letters. Never pass an empty name without decorative: it would be an image with no name.
docs.avatar.a11y.picture: The picture has an empty alt, because the avatar already has the name: it is announced once. Whether the picture shows or the initials do, the screen reader says the same.
docs.avatar.a11y.strings: Avatar has no text of its own: the name is yours, in the language of your page, and a FormaProvider changes nothing here.
docs.avatar.api.className: Added after the library's own class names, on the avatar.
docs.avatar.api.decorative: Hides the avatar from assistive technology, for when the name is already written next to it.
docs.avatar.api.name: The full name. It makes the initials and is the accessible name of the avatar.
docs.avatar.api.size: The size of the avatar: 28, 36 or 48 px, set by the tokens --avatar-size-small, --avatar-size-medium and --avatar-size-large.
docs.avatar.api.src: The URL of the picture. The initials show when it is missing or when it fails to load.
docs.avatar.api.tone: The color pair of the initials and their background, with the same roles as the tones of Badge.
docs.avatar.decorative.description: The name is written beside the avatar, so the avatar leaves the accessibility tree and nothing is read twice.
docs.avatar.decorative.hint: A screen reader reads the name once.
docs.avatar.decorative.title: Decorative
docs.avatar.initials.description: The initials are the first letter of the first word of the name and of the last one, in capitals: a middle name is skipped, and a name of one word gives one letter.
docs.avatar.initials.title: Initials
docs.avatar.limit.initials: The initials take the first character of a word as the browser counts it. A letter that is written as a base letter plus a combining accent loses the accent, an emoji or a letter outside the basic plane gives half a character, and «ß» becomes «SS». Names typed with accented letters as single characters, as most keyboards do, are fine.
docs.avatar.limit.interactive: An avatar is not a button or a link: it has no hover, focus or press behavior. Wrap it in a control of your own when it needs one, and name that control.
docs.avatar.limit.native: It takes only the props listed above: no id, title or data-* is forwarded. Put the attribute on a wrapper element.
docs.avatar.limit.retry: When a picture fails to load, the initials stay even if src later changes to a working URL. Give the avatar a key that includes the URL to try the new one.
docs.avatar.limit.sizes: There are three sizes, fixed by the tokens --avatar-size-small, --avatar-size-medium and --avatar-size-large. There is no prop or custom property for another size.
docs.avatar.limit.tones: There are five tones and no way to add one. The tone does not depend on the name: choose it yourself, and do not use it as the only sign of who someone is.
docs.avatar.picture.description: A picture fills the circle and covers it. When the link is missing or fails, the avatar shows the initials at the same size, so the layout does not move. The JSX names a file of your own.
docs.avatar.picture.failedHint: The picture fails to load: the initials show.
docs.avatar.picture.loadedHint: The picture loads and covers the circle.
docs.avatar.picture.title: Picture
docs.avatar.sizes.description: Three sizes, 28, 36 and 48 px. The default is medium.
docs.avatar.sizes.title: Sizes
docs.avatar.summary: A round picture of a person, or their initials when there is no picture.
docs.avatar.tones.description: Five color roles, the same as Badge. Each one is shown on a card, because the neutral avatar has the background of the panel. The default is blue.
docs.avatar.tones.title: Tones
docs.avatar.usage.description: Import Avatar and pass the full name: it makes the initials and names the avatar for a screen reader.
